background: We want to optimize the waste collection system for a city, taking full account of the city's particular characteristics. We want to find a collection truck route for each zone and minimize its length.
constraints: Each node in T is visited exactly once
The trucks directly service all block sides that are too long to be handled under the achique system
Impose that $t$ is the last node visited
Avoid violating traffic restrictions when passing from the end of one shortest path to the start of the next
Some paths of length three and four are forbidden and cannot be used
objective: Minimize the length of the route that visits each node in T exactly once

parameters.definition: The set of arcs representing one-way block sides
The set of edges representing two-way block sides
Each arc $(i,j)$ is weighted by the length of the block side it represents
Set of traffic restictions, for example if travel from $(i,j)\rightarrow (j,k)$ is forbidden, $(i,j,k)\in F$
Shortest path between i, j that has no forbidden paths as subpaths
Starting point for the truck is represented by $s \in V$
Arrival point for the truck is represented by $t \in V$
The complete digraph T=(V_T, A_T), where V_T=V_Z\cup\{s,t\} and the weight $w_{(i,j)} of arc $(i,j)$ is given by $\ell(\gamma_{(i,j)})$
The set of block sides that cannot be serviced under the achique system. \mathcal{L}={e in A_S \cup E_S: \ell(e) > 130}
For each $e \in \mathcal{L}$, $(i,j) \in A_T$ belongs to $L_e$ if any of the arcs representing $e$ are part of $\gamma_{(i,j)}$

For any $(i,j)\in V_T$, $i \neq j$, $V_{(i,j)}$ is the set of all $k \in V_T$ such that if $u$ is the second-to-last node in $\gamma_{(i,j)}$ and $v$ is the second node in $\gamma_{(j,k)}$, then $(u,j,v)\in F$
For each $\delta=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) \in F_4, v \in V_T$ belongs to $B_\delta$ if and only if the last arc in $\gamma_{v, u_2}$ is $(u_1,u_2)$
For each $\delta=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) \in F_4, v \in V_T$ belongs to $\hat{B}_\delta$ if and only if the two last arcs in $\gamma_{v, u_3}$ are $(u_1,u_2)$ and $(u_2,u_3)$
For each $\delta=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) \in F_4, v \in V_T$ belongs to $E_\delta$ if and only if the first arc in $\gamma_{u_3, v}$ is $(u_3,u_4)$
For each $\delta=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) \in F_4, v \in V_T$ belongs to $\hat{E}_\delta$ if and only if the two first arc in $\gamma_{u_2, v}$ are $(u_2,u_3)$ and $(u_3,u_4)$
